newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF defies oil well-capping order.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF defies oil well-capping order.

text.p: Argentina's oil giant YPF SA Thursday challenged a governmental order to cap all of its wells in two Patagonian fields due to recent spills, amid charges it violated international security norms.
YPF sought a court's ruling challenging the order to cap its wells in two provinces affected by oil spills it has put down to abnormal storms and provincial authorities to negligence by the firm.

The government Wednesday ordered YPF to close its 112 wells in the provinces of Neuquen and Mendoza after oil leakages in February and March flowed to the Colorado River that stretches 1,000 km (600 miles) across Patagonia.

YPF, Argentina's largest company, says the spills totaled just 25 cubic meters of crude, but authorities from Neuquen said thousands of cubic meters poured into the river, the area's main source of water.
The company said oil pumping stopped, adding it saw no reason to close wells it does not deem entail any risk for people or the environment.
"We sought Wednesday a court order in Buenos Aires to see whether the government has the right to ask for the closures," YPF's vice-President for Upstream Marcelo Guiscardo said.

"We have closed all the (52) wells in Desfiladero Bayo oil field," he told Reuters in a telephone interview from the town of Rincn de los Sauces in Neuquen, 850 miles (1,300 km) south west of Buenos Aires.
"But in Puerto Molina (field) we only capped seven, not the 60 the Energy Secretariat had requested, as we deemed there is no technical reason to close the rest."
However, Neuquen's Water and Health Office director Eduardo Muller charged YPF's oil pipelines were poorly built and in violation of international norms.

"Had the norms been taken into account there might perhaps have been only one accident, not as many and so recurrent," he said, adding several oil spills by YPF and other companies occurred in the past few years.
He also said YPF cannot hide behind unforseeable circumstances, saying the is area is known for its storms and rockslides.
